conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Joint BOCC/BOE Quarterly Meeting May 18, 2021 9:00 AM
conflicts.issue: DPS Budget Request Submission Deadline (April 1 vs. Mid-March) in Joint MOU
conflicts.summary: DPS MOU drafters proposed moving the school board's annual draft budget request to the county from mid-March to April 1, while County Budget Director Keith Lane urged keeping the mid-March timeline.
conflicts.side_a_position: Move the DPS draft budget request deadline in the joint MOU from mid-March to April 1.
side_a_arguments: Aligns the school district's budget preparation with the county's budget development cycle.
conflicts.side_b_position: Retain the mid-March deadline for DPS's initial budget request.
side_b_arguments: DPS funding is by far the county's largest budget allocation, and April 1 arrives after all other county department requests are already being compiled.
Moving two weeks later prevents county budget staff from comparing DPS needs alongside other county departments.
conflicts.resolution: After County Budget Director Keith Lane raised the timing concern, Chair Bettina Umstead agreed to amend the draft MOU back to the earlier mid-March date pending sign-off by Jovonia Lewis and Frederick Xavier Ravin III ahead of the next quarterly meeting.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Joint BOE/BOCC Quarterly Meeting November 16, 2021 9:00 AM
conflicts.issue: Framing of Escalating DPS Capital Improvement Plan Costs ('Tidal Wave' vs. Deferred Needs)
conflicts.summary: County budget officials framed the jump in five-year CIP requests from $400M to over $1B as an unaffordable 'tidal wave' requiring scrutiny of shovel-readiness and LGC/rating-agency capacity, while Dr. Mike Lee objected to rhetoric implying DPS was inflating requests rather than addressing overdue deferred maintenance and construction inflation.
conflicts.side_a_position: Highlight the rapid expansion of CIP spending requests as a fiscal 'tidal wave' exceeding historical spend patterns and potentially beyond county affordability without strict prioritization.
side_a_arguments: Five-year CIP requests climbed from $400M two years ago to over $1B, with DPS's 5-year request jumping from $110M to $352M.
The Local Government Commission (LGC) and bond rating agencies will scrutinize debt authorizations compared to historical spend capacity.
conflicts.side_b_position: Reject narratives suggesting DPS is padding or mismanaging its capital budget, emphasizing that cost growth stems from inflation, state underfunding, and compounding deferred facility needs.
side_b_arguments: Deferring school repairs causes nonlinear, exponential future cost increases ('future cost of money').
The DPS facility master plan reflects genuine, professionally vetted district survival needs rather than 'pork' or discretionary add-ons.
conflicts.resolution: County Manager Claudia Hager clarified the chart also reflected K-12 state underfunding and county project growth ($719M non-DPS), and both boards committed to reviewing debt-capacity and tax scenarios together ahead of February 2022.

conflicts.meeting_title: Durham Public Schools Joint BOCC/BOE Quarterly Meeting May 18, 2021 9:00 AM
conflicts.issue: Proposed Budget Indexing Formula in Joint BOCC/BOE MOU
conflicts.summary: Frederick Xavier Ravin III and the draft MOU proposed exploring a budget indexing formula for DPS funding, while another official cautioned against locking boards into a rigid formula without staff study.
conflicts.side_a_position: Establish a working indexing formula in the MOU to project expected school system funding needs.
side_a_arguments: Creates a more transparent and predictable budget development process for both boards and staff.
conflicts.side_b_position: Have mutual budget staffs thoroughly review or study any indexing formula for a year before adopting it.
side_b_arguments: Locking into a formula could prevent the boards from having deep, responsive discussions as community needs change.
conflicts.resolution: Deferred for joint budget staff review and feedback before finalizing the MOU at the next quarterly meeting.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Joint BOE/BOCC Quarterly Meeting November 16, 2021 9:00 AM
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education and Durham Board of County Commissioners held their November 16, 2021 quarterly joint meeting, unanimously approving the August 17, 2021 joint minutes via roll call before reviewing escalating 10-year Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) projections. County budget officials presented the combined five-year CIP request surging from $400 million to over $1 billion—calling it a 'tidal wave' driven by construction inflation, supply chain delays, and expanded DPS and county project scopes—which prompted pushback from Dr. Mike Lee against portraying DPS capital requests as excessive or mismanaged rather than overdue responses to deferred maintenance and state underfunding. Both boards also discussed factoring solar-ready and renewable energy costs into upcoming school construction, expanding capacity at a replacement Durham School of the Arts beyond 1,500 seats, and exploring joint disparity studies. After a brief five-minute Pre-K overview deferred for full discussion to February 2022, both boards approved the 2022 joint meeting schedule by roll call.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Agenda Review, and Approval of August 17, 2021 Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Bettina Umstead called the joint BOE/BOCC meeting to order with no agenda adjustments. County Commissioner Wendy Jacobs moved and Board Member Natalie Beyer seconded approving the August 17, 2021 joint meeting minutes, which passed unanimously via roll call across both boards (with Vice Chair Jovonia Lewis experiencing a brief audio issue on Zoom).

agenda_items.title: Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) Update (County and DPS)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: County officials presented a 'tidal wave' chart showing five-year total CIP requests growing from $400M (2020-24) to over $1B (2022-26), including DPS five-year projects rising from $110M to $352M and non-DPS county projects reaching $418M over five years ($719M over 10 years), citing labor shortages, inflation, LGC scrutiny, and state K-12 deferred maintenance. Dr. Mike Lee pushed back on the framing to counter public narratives of DPS fiscal mismanagement, emphasizing that capital needs grow exponentially when deferred. Boards also discussed incorporating solar/renewable energy costs, increasing Durham School of the Arts capacity above 1,500 (to address 1,800-1,900 enrollment), debt/tax modeling, and joint disparity studies with Dr. Julius Monk.

agenda_items.title: Pre-K Program Update (Abbreviated Overview)
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Due to time constraints, Chair Umstead asked Dr. Hardy, Dr. Pittman, Pre-K coordinator Thompson, and Linda Chappelle for a five-minute highlight of Pre-K enrollment and plans to add Pre-K classrooms through school renovations to ease proximity barriers. Full questions and presentation were deferred to the February 2022 joint meeting as the first agenda item.

agenda_items.title: 2022 Joint BOE/BOCC Meeting Schedule Approval and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: The boards considered the proposed 2022 joint meeting schedule beginning in February 2022. Natalie Beyer moved, seconded by Alexandra Valladares and Commissioner Nida Allam, and the schedule was approved by joint roll call vote before adjournment.

meetings.title: Joint Board of Education/Board of County Commissioners Quarterly Meeting August 17, 2021
meetings.executive_summary: The Durham Public Schools Board of Education and Durham Board of County Commissioners held their quarterly joint meeting remotely, hosted by the County Commissioners and chaired by BOCC Chair Brenda Howerton alongside DPS Chair Bettina Umstead. Following unanimous roll-call approval of the April 18, 2021 joint meeting minutes, DPS staff and Durham PreK partners presented an early learning update detailing expansion from 61 to 65 Pre-K classrooms (858 seats) in 2021-22 and 68 classrooms (914 seats) in 2022-23 with Lyons Farm Elementary, alongside equity, Child Find, and wraparound care barriers. DPS CFO Paul LeSieur reviewed the district's $169 million county allocation (including over $11 million in new funding for operations, $6 million in capital outlay, and $250 teacher supplement increases) alongside uncertain state General Assembly budget proposals and rising retirement, health insurance, hotspot, and Pre-K costs. Interim County Manager Claudia Hager and Budget Director Keith Lane then outlined the FY22-31 Capital Improvement Plan refresh and the timeline toward a November 8, 2022 General Obligation bond referendum amid 20-80% construction cost inflation and labor shortages, before Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga requested Sheriff/City traffic assistance and 7:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. community COVID testing sites for school reopening.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order, Roll Call, and Approval of April 18, 2021 Joint Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Durham County Clerk Monica Toomer confirmed a quorum of County Commissioners and DPS Board of Education members online, and BOCC Chair Brenda Howerton called the meeting to order at 9:00 a.m. with no agenda adjustments. After confirming two name corrections requested by BOCC Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs were included in the packet, the joint boards approved the April 18, 2021 minutes by roll call vote.

agenda_items.title: Early Learning and Pre-K Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy Superintendent Dr. Nakia Hardy, Dr. Suzanne Cotterman, and Durham PreK's Linda Chappell presented DPS early learning strategies, online and multilingual ESL enrollment outreach, and special/blended classroom growth from 61 classrooms (784 seats) to 65 classrooms (858 seats) in 2021-22 and 68 classrooms (914 seats) in 2022-23 at Lyons Farm Elementary. Officials also discussed incorporating Pre-K spaces into new school designs such as Elementary F, Child Find evaluations, equity assessment recommendations, and wraparound before- and after-care gaps.

agenda_items.title: DPS School Year and Budget Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS CFO Paul LeSieur thanked commissioners for over $11 million in new annual county funding—bringing total county support to $169 million, including $5.6 million for operations, $6 million for capital outlay, $500,000 for English learners, $250 certified staff supplement raises toward $5,600, and added custodial/counselor/equity positions, while noting roughly $31 million passes through to charter schools. LeSieur outlined pending state House/Senate budget differences (2.5-2.6% raises vs. Governor's 5%, ~22.8% retirement, >$7,000 health insurance, $15/hour minimum wage phase-in, and $15 million in potential technology forfeiture funds), and members discussed avoiding the 20% charter pass-through on Pre-K requests, $2 million hotspot costs, and school nurse vacancies.

agenda_items.title: Durham County Capital Improvement Plan (CIP) and 2022 GO Bond Referendum Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim County Manager Claudia Hager and Budget Director Keith Lane reviewed broadband ARPA/federal strategy and the FY22-FY31 10-year CIP update, noting half of the county's $60-70 million annual debt service supports DPS and warning of 20-80% construction cost inflation (100% steel and 375% lumber spikes) and supply/labor constraints. Lane walked through milestones leading to a November 8, 2022 General Obligation bond referendum, and officials discussed updating DPS facility needs, $40,000 in county funding added to The Institute's contract for MWBE construction outreach, carbon-reduction investments, and property tax rate pressures.

agenda_items.title: Public Comments Check, COVID-19 Reopening Coordination, and Adjournment
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Clerk Monica Toomer confirmed no citizens had signed up or submitted emails for public comment. DPS Chair Bettina Umstead thanked the county for its mask mandate, and Superintendent Dr. Pascal Mubenga requested Sheriff's Office and City traffic support during the first two weeks of school and expanded 7:00 a.m.-7:00 p.m. community COVID-19 testing sites before BOCC Chair Howerton noted the November 16, 2021 joint meeting and adjourned at 11:00 a.m.

votes.item_title: Approval of April 18, 2021 Joint BOE/BOCC Meeting Minutes
votes.notes: Joint BOCC/BOE roll call vote; Durham County Commissioners Nida Allam, Heidi Carter, Wendy Jacobs, and Chair Brenda Howerton also voted Yes. Dr. Mike Lee and Matt Sears were not named in the opening attendance or roll call.
votes.discussion_detail: After Clerk Monica Toomer confirmed two minor name revisions requested by BOCC Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs were in the packet, the joint meeting moved and seconded approval of the April 18, 2021 minutes (individual mover/seconder not named in the transcript). Clerk Toomer conducted a roll call of participating County Commissioners and the five participating DPS board members, all voting Yes.

meetings.title: Durham Public Schools Joint BOCC/BOE Quarterly Meeting May 18, 2021 9:00 AM
meetings.executive_summary: At the May 18, 2021 joint quarterly meeting of the Durham Public Schools Board of Education and the Durham Board of County Commissioners presided over by DPS Chair Bettina Umstead, the two boards unanimously approved revised February 16, 2021 joint meeting minutes (adding a member omitted from attendance). Interim County Manager Claudia Hager and Budget Director Keith Lane presented the FY21-22 Manager's Recommended Budget, proposing a 1-cent property tax increase (to 72.22 cents per $100 valuation) and $163.3 million in DPS funding—a 6.6% increase adding $8.9 million in current expense (including $1.9 million to sustain the $15/hour classified wage floor) and $1.13 million in capital outlay. In reviewing a draft joint Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) presented by DPS members Jovonia Lewis and Frederick Xavier Ravin III, officials debated inter-board communication protocols, aligning county budget performance metrics with DPS's strategic and racial equity plans, moving the DPS budget request deadline from mid-March to April 1, and creating a budget indexing formula. After County Budget Director Keith Lane warned that an April 1 deadline falls too late to synchronize with county department requests, Chair Umstead agreed to revert the draft MOU date to mid-March pending agreement from Lewis and Ravin, and officials requested joint staff review of the indexing proposal before finalizing the MOU next quarter.

agenda_items.title: Call to Order and Approval of February 16, 2021 Joint Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS Chair Bettina Umstead called the virtual joint BOCC/BOE meeting to order and reviewed the agenda. Following a board member's request to correct the February 16, 2021 joint meeting minutes to reflect her attendance, County Commissioner Wendy Jacobs moved approval with the correction (seconded by another Commissioner), passing unanimously by voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Durham County FY21-22 Manager's Recommended Budget Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Interim County Manager Claudia Hager and Budget Director Keith Lane reported $19.7 million in projected general fund natural revenue growth ($13.6M property tax, $6.1M sales tax) and $2.2 billion in tax base growth, proposing a 1-cent property tax rate increase from 71.22 to 72.22 cents per $100 valuation (~$4.58M-$4.6M total, or $20/year on a $200,000 home). The recommended budget allocates $163.3 million to Durham Public Schools—a 6.6% increase consisting of $8.9 million in new current expense funding (including $1.9 million to sustain $15/hour classified pay) and $1.13 million in new capital funding (raising capital outlay from $3.37M to $4.5M).

agenda_items.title: Joint BOCC/BOE Memorandum of Understanding (MOU) Revisions
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Board members Jovonia Lewis and Frederick Xavier Ravin III presented proposed updates to the BOCC/BOE MOU: avoiding unilateral commissioner political statements after joint meetings ('we don't answer to you, but we work with you'), aligning county budget narrative metrics with DPS's Strategic Plan, Racial Equity Action Plan (with Dr. Kelvin Bullock), EC priorities, and student climate surveys, shifting DPS's draft budget submission to April 1, and exploring a transparent budget indexing formula. County Budget Director Keith Lane objected to the April 1 deadline as too late for county budget compilation, prompting Chair Umstead to offer reverting to mid-March, while a member urged a year of staff study on indexing before locking boards into a formula.
agenda_items.vote_summary: Informational / Deferred to next quarterly meeting

votes.item_title: Approval of February 16, 2021 Joint BOCC/BOE Meeting Minutes (With Attendance Correction)
votes.notes: Joint BOCC/BOE voice vote; moved by BOCC Commissioner Wendy Jacobs and seconded by an unidentified County Commissioner.
votes.discussion_detail: After a female board member requested correcting the February 16, 2021 minutes to record her attendance, Durham County Commissioner Wendy Jacobs moved and another County Commissioner seconded approving the minutes with the revision. The joint boards approved the motion unanimously by voice vote.

meetings.title: Joint BOCC-BOE Meeting
meetings.executive_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton hosted and presided over the joint meeting of the Durham Board of County Commissioners and the Durham Public Schools Board of Education, opening with a unanimous voice vote approving the November 11, 2020 joint minutes as corrected. Co-chairs Judge Elaine O'Neal and Dr. Cohen presented the proposed Durham City-County Racial Equity Commission bylaws, prompting discussion on youth representation, equal elected-official participation across all three local boards, and budget-retreat timelines for funding stipends. Durham Public Schools administrators then briefed both boards on virtual learning, summer learning legislation in the General Assembly, Northern High School and Lions Farm Elementary capital projects, sustainability standards, and FY 2021-22 budget priorities including HB 90 class-size mandates, $6 million in annual maintenance needs, and staff compensation. During the Pre-K and Durham Head Start update, Chair Howerton and Commissioner Nimasheena Burns raised concerns about last-minute budget requests and emphasized that DPS leadership must coordinate earlier and respect the BOCC chair and budget process ahead of the May 18, 2021 joint meeting.

agenda_items.title: Agenda Review and Approval of November 11, 2020 Joint Meeting Minutes
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Chair Brenda A. Howerton reviewed the joint agenda and opened corrections for the November 11, 2020 minutes. Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs requested removing an erroneous 'Doctor' title next to Commissioner Heidi Carter's name. Following the correction, the joint boards approved the minutes by unanimous voice vote.

agenda_items.title: Durham City-County Racial Equity Commission Bylaws Discussion
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Co-chairs Judge Elaine O'Neal and Dr. Cohen discussed proposed bylaws for the Durham City-County Racial Equity Commission, emphasizing robust representation from Durham youth beyond DPS students. Commissioners and board members stressed acting promptly on stipends and budget allocations before upcoming budget retreats and ensuring equal representation of one or two elected officials from the City Council, BOCC, and School Board.

agenda_items.title: DPS Virtual Learning and Summer Learning Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Deputy Superintendent Dr. Hardy presented on virtual learning and plans for summer learning programs. Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs asked about federal and state funding for summer learning and safe reopening/staff vaccination, while Superintendent Dr. Mubenga and staff noted a newly filed General Assembly bill prescribing six weeks of summer learning using federal dollars without new state funding; Commissioner Nida Allam also asked about disaggregated demographic data on family preferences for virtual versus in-person instruction.

agenda_items.title: DPS Capital Projects, Sustainability, and MWBE/HUB Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS facilities staff reported construction progress on Northern High School (foundation and arts/cafeteria wing) and Lions Farm Elementary within the $508 million prioritized capital needs from 2019, alongside sustainability design standards. In follow-up remarks, a commissioner urged the boards to budget for dedicated MWBE/HUB expertise rather than treating minority- and women-owned business participation as a checkbox, noting a March session with Tammy Hall on the HUB process.

agenda_items.title: DPS FY 2021-22 Budget Presentation
agenda_items.discussion_summary: DPS leadership outlined upcoming FY 2021-22 budget pressures, including stricter HB 90 K-3 class size caps, $6 million needed annually for ongoing maintenance rather than lump-sum capital allocations, counselors and behavioral support staff, and sustaining the $15-per-hour minimum wage ($3.8 million) alongside potential staff raises. Officials also discussed state revenue reserves ($4 billion) and uncollected fines and forfeitures ($750 million statewide), and Board member Lewis asked about the spring digital access study and 1-to-1 IT refresh.

agenda_items.title: Pre-K Expansion and Durham Head Start Update
agenda_items.discussion_summary: Dr. Debbie Pittman and Head Start representative Linda reported growth in serving preschoolers with disabilities and Head Start's mixed in-person and virtual delivery launched in January despite tight classroom ratios under COVID-19. In closing remarks, Commissioner Nimasheena Burns and Chair Brenda A. Howerton cautioned DPS to submit prioritized funding lists earlier and communicate directly through the BOCC Chair rather than bypassing leadership ahead of the May 18, 2021 joint meeting.

votes.notes: Joint BOCC-BOE voice vote; mover and seconder were not named in transcript audio, and all five seated BOCC commissioners participated in the meeting without dissent.
votes.discussion_detail: Minutes were amended per Vice Chair Wendy Jacobs's request to remove an erroneous 'Doctor' reference attached to Commissioner Heidi Carter's name.
